correctness.rationale: The primary finite-graph circulation theorem turns rainbow-triangle absence into all-zero extinction; every induced four-cycle is coned to a third part, so triangles detect integer circulation. A rainbow triangle forces the maximal 1/3 excitation rate, hence eventual global color rotation and primitive period three. A three-color Hall obstruction shows the only additional no-rainbow colorings beyond at-most-two-color configurations are exactly 6r. On recurrent rotations, every forbidden missing-neighbor event corresponds to a unique color singleton whose mate bears the previous color; \(6r(4^{r-1}-1)\) such disjoint events are removed from surjective colorings. Algebra and critical event disjointness checked independently. The accompanying complete state enumerators (C++ \(r=3\)..7 and independently Python \(r=3\)..5) reproduce every claimed basin and orbit count; no infinite conclusion rests on finite experiments.

value.rationale: The complement of a perfect matching is a canonical vertex-transitive infinite graph family, with two natural global dynamical observables: extinction probability and count of primitive temporal three-cycles. The theorem computes both exactly for every \(r\ge4\) via structural Hall and singleton-mate obstruction counts, revealing that extinction decays as \(3(4/9)^r\) and that almost all configurations are eventually and immediately periodic. It is an all-size classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a trivial recomputation of an existing graph-general statement. The unproved entry-time spectrum is expressly excluded.
